fetched.title: Pylon MCP server: connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor
fetched.text:
# Pylon MCP server

Connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor to Pylon. Work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base with the permissions you already have.

Thank you! Your submission has been received!

Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form.

Trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers globally

What is Pylon’s MCP server?

Deploy AI agents that handle questions end-to-end, gather context for your team, and escalate to humans when it matters.

Can ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor use Pylon data?

Yes. Point a supported MCP client at your regional Pylon MCP URL, sign in with OAuth or use an API token, and work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base from the AI tool you already use. For ChatGPT, you can also install Pylon’s native ChatGPT app from Settings > Plugins (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins). See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

Is access scoped to each user?

Yes. Every action runs as the authenticated user. The server cannot return data that user cannot see in Pylon, or write changes that user cannot already make in the UI. Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

Can engineers investigate from their editor?

Yes. Tools like Claude Code or Cursor can open a Pylon issue, pull message history, and keep working in the same flow your team already uses for debugging. Opening a pull request still depends on that coding tool’s own GitHub or codebase connection, not on a Pylon MCP "create PR" tool.

Can you turn support evidence into docs and analysis?

Yes. Feed issue context into an AI tool to draft an internal note, a product brief, or an account summary, and combine Pylon data with other sources those tools can reach (for example Notion or Linear) when those connections are configured.

How do you set up the Pylon MCP server?

Step 1

Enable MCP Access

Make sure each user or API token identity that connects has the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard.

Step 2

Open the MCP Server settings in Pylon

In Pylon, go to Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server. Copy your workspace’s regional MCP URL from Installation.

Step 3

Connect your AI tool

Add the URL in your AI tool’s MCP settings, or for ChatGPT install the Pylon app from Settings > Plugins. Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP (stateless).

US server: mcp.usepylon.com

EU server: mcp.eu.usepylon.com

See Pylon’s MCP docs for the full tool list.

See the MCP setup guide for client steps.

See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

See how to connect Pylon to Claude with MCP.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Pylon MCP server?

MCP is an open standard that lets AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external products. Pylon’s MCP server exposes your Pylon workspace (issues, accounts, contacts, and more) to those tools over OAuth 2.0 or an API token, so your team can query and act on support data from the AI clients they already use.

Which AI tools can connect to Pylon via MCP?

Pylon’s MCP server works with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor. For ChatGPT, the fastest path is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app; you can also add the regional MCP URL as a custom connector. Headless workers, scripts, and clients that support custom authorization headers can connect with an existing Pylon API token instead of OAuth.

What actions can an AI tool take in Pylon through MCP?

Connected AI tools can search and update issues, post internal notes, and send customer replies, which AI tools are instructed to show you for approval before sending. They can also manage accounts and contacts, draft and publish knowledge base articles, and work with macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, account notes, and call recordings require Account Intelligence. Feature requests and some other tools require additional plan features. All actions stay within your Pylon permissions.

Is the Pylon MCP server secure?

Connections use OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token’s identity, with that identity’s current role and permissions. No extra permissions are granted. The identity also needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

How do I set up the Pylon MCP server?

Open Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server in Pylon, copy your regional URL (https://mcp.usepylon.com or https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com), and add it in your AI tool (or install the ChatGPT app). Sign in with OAuth, or send an existing API token in an Authorization: Bearer header if your client supports it.

Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan?

Yes. The pricing Features by tier table lists the Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some individual MCP tools still require add-ons or plan features such as Account Intelligence.

fetched.title: Authentication | Pylon
fetched.text:
The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard.

### API regions

Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted:

* US region: https://api.usepylon.com
* EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com

Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted.

You can tell a token's region from its prefix:

Prefix

Region

`pylon_api_eu_`

EU

`pylon_api_`

US

Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns `401` with the `wrong_region_token` error code, and the message names the correct URL.

Once you've created a token, call the `/me` endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works.

## Create an API token

Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.

1. Go to **Settings > Integrations & dev > API**. On the **Tokens** tab, click **Create API Token**.
2. Enter a **Name**.
3. Choose who the token acts as:

   * Leave **Act as user or bot (optional)** empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a **Role** to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon.
   * Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions.
4. Optionally, add an **IP allowlist** (see below).
5. Click **Create** and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once.

Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes.

### Roles

A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with **Edit**. Older tokens that have no role act as Admin.

A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do.

See Roles and user management for what each role allows.

### Who actions are attributed to

* **Token with its own identity:** actions show up under the token's name and icon.
* **Token that acts as a user or bot:** actions are attributed to that user or bot.

### Bots

Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon.

To create one, go to **Settings > Workspace > Users**, open the **Bots** tab, and click **New Bot**. Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under **Act as user or bot** when you create a token.

### IP allowlist

Add IP addresses (for example `203.0.113.10`) or CIDR blocks (for example `203.0.113.0/24`) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP.

Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16` never match.

A request from an address that isn't on the list returns `401` with the `invalid_api_token` error code.

## Manage tokens

The **Tokens** tab shows each token's **Acts as**, **Token preview**, **Role**, **Created by**, **Last used**, and **Created** values. From the **…** menu on a token you can:

* **Edit:** change the name, role, or IP allowlist.
* **Duplicate Token:** create a new token with the same settings.
* **Rotate:** generate a new token value. The current token stops working immediately.
* **Delete:** permanently revoke the token. Calls using it stop working immediately.
* **View Activity:** open the token's request logs.

## Review API request logs

Only Admins can view request logs. Go to **Settings > Integrations & dev > API** and open the **Logs** tab, or choose **View Activity** from a token's **…** menu to see only that token's requests.

Filter by token, or choose **All tokens**, and by a date range of up to 90 days. The range defaults to the last 7 days. Each request shows when it was made, the token, who it acted as, the method, endpoint, response status, source IP, user agent, and request ID. Requests made with a token that was since deleted still appear.

Requests rejected for authentication or rate limits aren't logged, and older requests may not show a token.

### When tokens are revoked automatically

When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes:

* every API token that user created, and
* every API token that acts as that user.

Before you deactivate someone who created tokens your integrations rely on, create replacement tokens from another Admin's account.

An Admin who has created Admin-role tokens can't be moved to a different role until those tokens are deleted.

NextAPI conventions

fetched.text:
For the complete documentation index, see llms.txt. This page is also available as Markdown.

These rules apply across Pylon's API. The API reference lists each endpoint's parameters; this page explains how they behave.

## Requests and responses

* Send request bodies as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`. The one exception is `POST /attachments`, which takes `multipart/form-data`.
* Successful responses put the result in `data` and include a `request_id`. List and search responses also include `pagination`.
* Unknown fields are ignored, not rejected. A misspelled field name is silently dropped, so check the field names in the reference.
* Sending `null` for an optional field is the same as leaving it out.

## IDs

Most endpoints take Pylon IDs. A few path parameters also accept another identifier:

Path

Accepts

`/issues/{id}` and its sub-paths

Issue ID or issue number

`/accounts/{id}`, and account activities, highlights, and files

Account ID or account external ID

`/contacts/{id}`

Contact ID or contact external ID

See External IDs for attaching your own identifiers to accounts.

## Timestamps

* Every timestamp uses RFC 3339, for example `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z` or `2026-10-01T09:00:00+02:00`. A timezone (`Z` or an offset) is required.
* Responses return timestamps in UTC to the second, for example `2026-10-01T14:03:27Z`.
* In query strings, encode `+` as `%2B` or use `Z`. An unencoded `+` is read as a space, and the request fails with `400`.

List and search endpoints use cursor pagination.

1. Send a `limit` (optional). Leave out `cursor` for the first page.
2. If the response has `pagination.has_next_page: true`, send `pagination.cursor` as `cursor` in the next request, with the same filter and other parameters.
3. Stop when `pagination` is missing or `has_next_page` is `false`.

`GET` endpoints take `cursor` and `limit` as query parameters. `POST .../search` endpoints take them in the JSON body. Treat cursors as opaque.

Limits vary by endpoint and are listed on each endpoint's `limit` parameter. Most search endpoints default to 100 results and accept up to 1,000. `GET /issues` defaults to and allows up to 20,000.

## Listing issues by time

`GET /issues` requires a time window:

Question

Answer

Which field is filtered?

The issue's `created_at`.

Are the bounds inclusive?

`start_time` is inclusive. `end_time` is exclusive.

Are both required?

Yes. Leaving either out returns `400`.

Maximum window

365 days between `start_time` and `end_time`.

Order

Newest `created_at` first.

Page size

`limit` defaults to 20,000, the maximum.

To filter on another timestamp, such as `updated_at`, `resolved_at`, or `latest_message_activity_at`, use `POST /issues/search`. Search has no maximum window:

## Search filters

Every `POST .../search` endpoint except feature requests takes a `filter` object with the same structure.

Key

Use

`operator`

Required unless the filter sets `related_object`. See the operators below.

`field`

The field to compare. Required unless `operator` is `and` or `or`.

`value`

A single value, for operators that take one.

`values`

An array, for operators that take several.

`subfilters`

An array of filters. Only used with `and` and `or`.

`related_object`

Matches on a related object, such as an issue's account. See Filter on a related object.

Combine conditions with `and` and `or`:

* A filter can be at most **3 levels deep**, counting the top-level filter. The example above uses all 3.
* In the example, `priority` is a custom field slug. Custom fields are filtered by slug, like built-in fields.
* `and` and `or` must have `subfilters` and can't have a `field` or `value`.
* Use `value` or `values` according to the operator. Sending the other one returns `400`.

### Filter on a related object

To match on a field of a related object, such as an issue's account or requester, put a `related_object` in place of a condition. `relationship` names the related object and `filter` is the condition it must match:

Endpoint

Relationship

Related object

Requires

`POST /issues/search`

`account`

Account

Account read

`requester`

Contact

Contact read

`assignee`

User

User read

`POST /contacts/search`

`account`

Account

Account read

`POST /accounts/search`

`owner`

User

User read

`POST /tasks/search`

`account`

Account

Account read

`project`

Project

Task management read

`assignee`

User

User read

`POST /projects/search`

`account`

Account

Account read

* A filter with `related_object` sets nothing else: no `operator`, `field`, `value`, `values`, or `subfilters`.
* `related_object.filter` uses the fields, operators, and custom field slugs of the related object's own search endpoint, listed in Allowed fields. Every one of those fields works, including account `account_id` and `tags`. Project `is_archived` takes `true` or `false`.
* To check several conditions on the same related object, make `related_object.filter` an `and` or `or` group.
* A `related_object` can't contain another `related_object`. It doesn't count toward the depth limit.
* Each relationship needs the read permission of the related object, without restrictions. Without it, the request returns `403`.
* Dotted paths such as `account.name` aren't supported. The error message shows the `related_object` form to use instead.
* Ticket form visibility conditions (`fields[].visibility_conditions[].filter` from `GET /ticket-forms`) use this format, and can contain `related_object` with the issue relationships `account`, `requester`, and `assignee`. A condition this format can't express, such as a hop through a relationship custom field, a chain of hops, or a value relative to the viewer, has `filter_unsupported: true` and no `filter`.

### Operators

Operator

Takes

Matches when the field...

`equals` / `not_equals`

`value`

is / isn't exactly the value

`in` / `not_in`

`values`

is / isn't one of the values

`contains` / `does_not_contain`

`value`

has / doesn't have the value (multi-value fields such as `tags`)

`includes_all_of`

`values`

has every value (multi-value fields)

`string_contains` / `string_does_not_contain`

`value`

contains / doesn't contain the text

`starts_with` / `ends_with`

`value`

starts / ends with the text

`time_is_after` / `time_is_before`

`value` (RFC 3339)

is strictly after / before the time

`time_range`

`values`: `[start, end]`

is between the two times, including both ends

`greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equals`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equals`

`value`

compares numerically

`is_set` / `is_unset`

nothing

has / doesn't have a value

### Allowed fields

Each search endpoint accepts its own fields, and each field allows only some operators. The full field-and-operator table is in the endpoint's description in the API reference. An invalid filter, such as one with an unknown field or a disallowed operator, returns `400` with code `invalid_filter`. The response lists every problem in the filter, each with its location and, where possible, the closest valid field, operator, or value. See Filter errors.

Endpoint

Built-in fields

Custom fields

`search_text`

`POST /issues/search`

`created_at`, `updated_at`, `resolved_at`, `latest_message_activity_at`, `state`, `tags`, `subject`, `body_html`, `account_id`, `requester_id`, `assignee_id`, `team_id`, `follower_user_id`, `follower_contact_id`, `ticket_form_id`, `issue_type`, `issue_is_issue_group`, `customer_portal_visible`, `reopened`, `slack_channel_id`, `workspace_email`

Yes

`POST /accounts/search`

`account_id`, `name`, `domains`, `tags`, `external_ids`, `owner_id`

Yes

Yes

`POST /contacts/search`

`id`, `email`, `name`, `account_id`

Yes

`POST /users/search`

No

`POST /custom-objects/{type}/search`

`name`, `account`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

Yes

`POST /tasks/search`

`account_id`, `project_id`, `status`, `assignee_id`, `milestone_id`, `created_at`, `due_date`, `updated_at`

Yes

No

`POST /projects/search`

`account_id`, `status`, `owner_id`, `is_archived`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

Yes

`POST /milestones/search`

`project_id`, `account_id`, `due_date`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `started_at`, `completed_at`

No

No

`POST /call-recordings/search`

`account_id`, `source`, `title`, `start_time`

No

No

`POST /surveys/search`

`updated_at`

No

No

`POST /audit-logs/search`

`action`, `action_happened_at`, `object_id`

No

No

`POST /feature-requests/search` doesn't take a `filter`. It takes `query`, `request_statuses`, `account_ids`, and `limit`.

Some fields also accept an earlier name: account `id` for `account_id`, and issue `title` for `subject`. Responses and error messages use the current names.

`search_text` runs a fuzzy text search. When you also send a `filter`, results must match both.

### Values to use

* `state`**:** `new`, `waiting_on_you`, `waiting_on_customer`, `on_hold`, `closed`, or a custom status slug.
* `tags`**:** the tag name.
* **Custom fields:** set `field` to the field's slug. For select and multi-select fields, use option slugs as values. See Find slugs.

Operators for a custom field depend on its type:

Custom field type

Operators

Text, URL, Email, Select

`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `string_contains`, `string_does_not_contain`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_set`, `is_unset`

Number

`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equals`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equals`, `is_set`, `is_unset`

Date, Datetime

`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `time_is_after`, `time_is_before`, `time_range`, `is_set`, `is_unset`

Multi-select

`contains`, `does_not_contain`, `in`, `not_in`, `includes_all_of`, `is_set`, `is_unset`

True/False, User, Contact, Relationship

`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `is_set`, `is_unset`

## Updating records

`PATCH` endpoints change only the fields you send.

* **Omitted fields don't change.** `null` counts as omitted.
* **Arrays replace the whole list.** Send the complete list you want, not just additions. Send `[]` to clear it.
* **Clear a reference with an empty string.** For example, `"assignee_id": ""` unassigns an issue.
* `custom_fields` **updates only the fields you list.** Other custom fields keep their values. For a multi-select field, `values` replaces the current selection. To clear a field, send its `slug` with no `value` or `values`.

Endpoint

Field

Behavior

`PATCH /issues/{id}`

`tags`

Replaces all tags on the issue.

`assignee_id`, `team_id`, `requester_id`

`""` removes the value.

`PATCH /accounts/{id}`

`channels`

Replaces the linked channels. Channels you leave out are unlinked from the account.

`domains`, `primary_domain`

Replaces the domains. `primary_domain` must be in `domains`.

`tags`, `external_ids`

Replaces the list.

`subaccount_ids`

Replaces the subaccounts. Accounts you leave out stop being subaccounts.

`owner_id`

`""` removes the owner.

`PATCH /accounts` (bulk)

`tags`

Set `tags_apply_mode` to `replace` (default), `append_only`, or `remove_only`.

`PATCH /contacts/{id}`

`email`

Replaces all of the contact's emails with this one.

`emails`, `phone_numbers`, `external_ids`

Replaces the list.

`account_id`

`""` removes the contact from its account.

`PATCH /teams/{id}`

`user_ids`

Replaces the team's members.

`PATCH /knowledge-bases/{id}/articles/{article_id}`

`tag_ids`

Replaces the article's tags.

### Updating knowledge base articles

* `body_html` saves a new **draft**. The published article doesn't change until you publish.
* To publish the new body in the same request, also send `"publish_updated_body_html": true` or `"is_published": true`.
* `"is_published": false` unpublishes the article.
* `title`, `is_unlisted`, `visibility_config`, `collection_id`, and `author_user_id` apply to the live article right away.
* To update a translation, add `language`. The same draft and publish rules apply.

## Files and attachments

### Upload a file

`POST /attachments` takes `multipart/form-data` with these fields:

Field

Required

Description

`file`

One of `file` or `file_url`

The file to upload. One file per request.

`file_url`

One of `file` or `file_url`

A URL Pylon downloads the file from.

`description`

No

A description of the file.

The response's `data` has the file's `id`, `name`, `url`, and `description`. Pass `url` in `attachment_urls` when you create an issue, reply, or internal note.

* Files up to 100 MB are supported. Larger files can be rejected with `413`; share those as a link instead. Email and chat channels may have smaller limits.
* Executables and script files are rejected with `400`.
* `attachment_urls` also accepts any publicly reachable URL. Pylon downloads the file and stores its own copy.

### Download a file

An issue's `attachment_urls` lists the files on its messages. Each message from `GET /issues/{id}/messages` has its files in `file_urls`.

* Most of these are signed links. Download them with a plain `GET`, without an `Authorization` header.
* They don't expire, so you can store them. Anyone with a link can download the file, so treat links as sensitive.
* Use the URL exactly as returned. Changing it invalidates the signature.
* Some older attachments return the URL they were originally stored with.

## Find slugs

The API refers to custom fields, select options, and statuses by slug, not by label.

Slug

In Pylon

Through the API

Custom field

The **API Slug** column on field settings pages, such as **Settings > Issue data > Fields** and **Settings > Account data > Fields**

`GET /custom-fields?object_type=issue` returns `slug`

Select option

**View and edit slugs** in the field's **…** menu

`select_metadata.options[].slug` in the same response

Issue status

—

`GET /issue-statuses` returns `slug`

User status

—

`GET /user-statuses` returns `slug`

`object_type` can be `account`, `issue`, `contact`, `task`, `project`, `meeting`, or `opportunity`. If you change a slug, update every integration that uses the old one.

Some slugs are reserved because they match built-in field names, for example account `state`, `source`, and `account_id`, and issue `subject`. If you send a reserved slug in `slug` when creating a custom field, the request is rejected. If you leave `slug` out and the field's label would produce a reserved slug, Pylon adds a number, for example `state_1`.

### Get all contacts

get/contacts

Returns a paginated list of contacts for the organization.

**Rate limit:** 300 requests per minute

Authorizations

AuthorizationstringRequired

Authorization: Bearer

Query parameters

cursorstringOptional

The cursor to use for pagination.

limitinteger · int64Optional

The number of contacts to fetch. Defaults to 100. Must be greater than 0 and less than 1000.

Responses

200Success

application/json

The request ID for tracking.

400

The request was invalid or could not be completed.

application/json

The request could not be authenticated for this API.

application/json

application/json

application/json

The request exceeded the applicable rate limit.

application/json

application/json


### Create a new contact

post/contacts

Creates a new contact with the specified email and optional metadata.

**Rate limit:** 300 requests per minute

Authorizations

AuthorizationstringRequired

Authorization: Bearer

Body

account\_external\_idstringOptional

The external ID of the account that this contact belongs to. Cannot be used together with account\_id.

account\_idstringOptional

The account that this contact belongs to.

avatar\_urlstringOptional

The avatar URL of the contact. Must be a square .png, .jpg or .jpeg.

emailstringOptional

The email of the contact.

namestringRequired

The name of the contact.

phone\_numbersstring[]Optional

The phone numbers of the contact. Must contain only digits 0-9, optionally preceded by + (E.164, e.g. +4365446231), and be 15 digits or less. Include the + and country code for non-US numbers; a 10-digit number without + is treated as US.

portal\_rolestringOptional

The portal role to assign to the contact. If not provided uses the default portal role from the portal settings.

Known values: `no_access`, `member`, `admin`. This list is not exhaustive.

portal\_role\_idstringOptional

The ID of the custom portal role to assign to the contact. Takes precedence over portal\_role if provided.

### Merge contacts

Merges a contact into a surviving contact. Both contacts must belong to the same account, unless the merged contact has no account, in which case it is first moved to the surviving contact's account. Issues, emails, phone numbers, survey responses, and other associated data are then transferred to the surviving contact, and the merged contact is permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.

**Rate limit:** 30 requests per minute
